item.description:
Added

  • **Headless application updates use a protected launchd broker.** The app publishes one owner-only typed request; a root-owned helper in /Library/PrivilegedHelperTools wakes through the system launchd domain, applies only Spire's signed pull update, and returns a durable root-authored receipt. Request UUID, expected build, file ownership, permissions, age, and single-flight execution are all validated before the updater runs.
  • **Build 331 has a bounded one-generation migration inside the Fleet window.** Spire accepts only King's exact paired source and management digests, copies the exact hashed signed updater into protected helper storage, re-verifies its ownership, digest, and code signature, and invokes only the fixed update operation before rebinding the peer to newly observed bytes.

Corrected

  • **Root no longer executes an application descendant or trusts update keys from an administrator-writable directory.** The protected updater carries immutable production feed, EdDSA, bundle, and Developer ID Team anchors, and reinstalls the model daemon in-process after the atomic swap. The replacement helper is copied into protected storage for the next run.
  • **A scheduled updater cannot terminate itself during the application swap.** Replacement launchd definitions are written without unloading the active updater process tree; ordinary remote calls retain their short deadline while the explicitly confirmed update receives time for download, signature checks, service recovery, and a terminal receipt.
  • **Interrupted application swaps recover before new work is accepted.** The protected helper holds one root-owned lock across startup recovery, brokered requests, and scheduled checks; an atomic, fsync-backed transaction journal precedes every destructive swap or rollback step. Restart recovery proves the exact signed old or new bundle and live service health before it publishes the request-bound terminal receipt and clears the journal.
  • **A nonempty launchd queue can never become an accidental scheduled update.** Fresh atomic writes defer, while stale staging files, malformed names, linked objects, and other persistent junk move one at a time into a root-only quarantine with a structured diagnostic. The helper performs a scheduled feed check only after a locked physical-empty observation.
